planting.note: Set out rooted divisions or nursery plugs in spring, since 'Flore Pleno' rarely sets viable seed and is propagated vegetatively to keep its fully double flowers true; plant into well-drained soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Plant divisions into well-drained soil and water them in well, then let the low, apple-scented foliage knit into a dense mat over the season. Unlike the single-flowered species, 'Flore Pleno' produces fully double, button-like white blooms that are especially prized for drying into chamomile tea and for scenting chamomile lawns and garden seats. It tolerates light foot traffic and releases a sweet, fruity fragrance when brushed or mown, but it flowers less heavily in deep shade or overly rich soil. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or plugs in spring into consistently moist to wet soil, since seed germination is slow and unreliable and most growers establish new plantings vegetatively.

directions: Plant divisions into damp, low-lying soil near a pond edge, ditch, or consistently irrigated bed, since this native grass naturally grows in moist meadows and spreads by shallow rhizomes to form a loose colony. It tolerates full sun in reliably wet ground but appreciates part shade where soil dries out more. The blades carry a sweet vanilla-like fragrance, especially when cut and dried, and have long been braided and burned in Indigenous North American ceremonies, woven into baskets, and steeped as a fragrant herbal tea or used to flavor bison-grass-style spirits. Divide and replant crowded clumps every few years to keep the planting vigorous.
